explanation: The superposition principle says overlapping waves add point-by-point: y = y₁ + y₂. For two equal-amplitude waves differing by phase φ, the resultant amplitude is 2A|cos(φ/2)| — maximum 2A when φ = 0 (constructive) and zero when φ = π (destructive). On the AP exam a phase difference of φ = 2π·(Δpath/λ) links to path difference, and integer-vs-half-integer multiples of λ select constructive vs destructive interference. The animation overlays the two source waves and their bright sum, with dashed lines marking the live resultant amplitude as the phase slider sweeps from in-phase to out-of-phase.
bullets: Waves add algebraically: the bright curve is y₁ + y₂ at every point.
φ = 0 gives constructive interference, resultant amplitude 2A.
φ = π gives destructive interference, resultant amplitude ≈ 0.
